data.source_title: Retrospective Audit of Medication Order Turnaround Time after Implementation of Standardized Definitions
data.locator: Table 2, “Turnaround Times for Medication Orders”; Methods, audit periods/turnaround definitions; Results.
data.source_setting: 231-bed community hospital, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada; acute medical-surgical, mental health and family-medicine inpatients; pharmacy orders processed 07:00–21:00.
data.source_period: Baseline: May 2009. Post-intervention: 28 randomly selected days, Aug 17–Oct 9, 2009.
data.source_n: 7,787 baseline prescriptions and 5,365 post-intervention prescriptions audited; eligible urgent-designation subsets: stat/emergent n=30 and 37; urgent/now n=54 and 105.
data.quantity: Stat/emergent order prescribing-to-dispensary-departure turnaround, median before/after definitions
data.source_evidence_basis: Retrospective audit; Table 2 median dispensary turnaround time for 30 baseline and 37 post-intervention stat/emergent orders. DTAT endpoint is order leaving dispensary, distinguished from total time until administration. The table prints 28 (90%) for 28/30; arithmetic on the printed count gives 93.3%, so retain both the paper-reported percentage and the count discrepancy explicitly.
data.limitations: One Canadian inpatient pharmacy; restricted to orders received in normal operating hours; before/after education study with small urgent subsets; no significant change observed (p=0.27). Table 2 has a count/percentage discrepancy for baseline stat/emergent orders: 28/30 calculates to 93.3%, while the article prints 90%. Preserve the reported text and raw numerator/denominator; do not silently substitute the recalculated value.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as an external urgent medication dispensing-stage comparator for inpatient-style pharmacy workflow; not a medication administration or ED prescription-to-bed endpoint.

data.source_title: Retrospective Audit of Medication Order Turnaround Time after Implementation of Standardized Definitions
data.locator: Table 2, rows “No. (%) with dispensary turnaround time < 15 min”; Results
data.source_setting: 231-bed community hospital, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada; acute medical-surgical, mental health and family-medicine inpatients; pharmacy orders processed 07:00–21:00.
data.source_period: Baseline: May 2009. Post-intervention: 28 randomly selected days, Aug 17–Oct 9, 2009.
data.source_n: 7,787 baseline prescriptions and 5,365 post-intervention prescriptions audited; eligible urgent-designation subsets: stat/emergent n=30 and 37; urgent/now n=54 and 105.
data.quantity: Urgent-designation orders with dispensary turnaround under 15 minutes, before/after definitions
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed audit counts and percentages reported in Table 2; full urgency-group denominators shown. The table prints 28 (90%) for 28/30; arithmetic on the printed count gives 93.3%, so retain both the paper-reported percentage and the count discrepancy explicitly.
data.limitations: Not a universal service-level target and reflects dispensary departure, not bedside availability; single-site workload and business hours. Authors report at least 90% combined urgent orders met the <15-min metric at baseline/post, but group-specific rounding differs. Table 2 has a count/percentage discrepancy for baseline stat/emergent orders: 28/30 calculates to 93.3%, while the article prints 90%. Preserve the reported text and raw numerator/denominator; do not silently substitute the recalculated value.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Could inform a candidate pharmacy-stage service-level scenario, with explicit uncertainty and local replacement criteria; do not treat as a promised target or whole medication turnaround.
